title: Writing "'Tain't What You Do" with Sy Oliver
summary: He hummed a tune from a Chicago drinking spot and wrote the song with Sy Oliver one Sunday in Nashville.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: And later on he and I became very close friends. We became roommates on that band. And so, one Sunday we were in Nashville and I was humming a little thing that I used to always hum around Chicago. You know, we used to sneak out drinking in Chicago when I was with Earl. And liquor wasn't legal then, you know, back there then, you know.

So, this guy used to serve liquor in teacups. And we used to -- I used to always kid him about it. His name was Ike. So, I made up a little thing. (Sings) "The--taint what'cha do--way h'atcha do it" (unintelligible) and a little thing like -- we used to kid him. So, Sy heard me humming that one day and he said, let's make a song out of that. I said ok. So, one sunday in Nashville we weren't working, and he and I sat down -- there was a piano in the lady's house and we got fooling around with it. And that's when we made up that tune "It taint what you do, it's the way how you do it." (up-to-date)
